#3599. GTA 6 Sets Even More Records

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some big numbers that speak to the pent-up demand. GTA 6 sold more than 30 million copies and hit almost $4 billion on day one, but that's just the start of understanding the impact of the game's release.

For starters, the internet service provider Comcast announced that November 18--the final day of preloading--was the busiest day in the company's history in terms of demand. Peak traffic was 31% higher than an average day and a full 9.6% higher that the previous biggest day ever for traffic to Comcast's network.

GTA 6 also now holds five of the top 10 busiest days of Comcast's network of all time. Going further, Comcast said around 24% of all internet traffic on Comcast's network was people downloading or playing GTA 6 on November 18 (no doubt thanks to the New Zealand trick). Additionally, traffic to Twitch on Comcast's network was up by almost 50% and "is still increasing," Comcast said.

A spokesperson for Comcast further contextualized the traffic data, telling GameSpot that between when preloading began on November 10 and through November 18, PlayStation and Xbox traffic pushed enough data on the network for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K repeatedly for two days straight.

Comcast was among the internet service providers that offered free speed boosts to subscribers to help them download GTA 6 faster.

Additionally, Mat Piscatella of Circana shared data that speaks to the enormity of GTA 6's launch on PlayStation and Xbox. For active accounts November 19 in the US, 61% of PS5 accounts "engaged with" GTA 6. On Xbox, 56% of Xbox players globally did. PS5 players averaged 513 minutes of play for GTA 6 on November 19, compared to 494 on Xbox.

These daily active user and minutes played figures are "absolutely bonkers," Piscatella said. GTA 6 was No. 1 on November 19, pushing Fortnite down to No. 2 based on these engagement metrics, Circana said.

For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

Actor Michael C. Hall has reacted to how GTA 6 features references to his Miami-set TV show Dexter, in which he famously played the serial killer Dexter.

Appearing on the Barstool Movies show, Hall said he was "informed" of the Easter eggs in GTA 6 about his character. "I wasn't consulted," he said with a laugh. "It's pretty cool to feel like [Dexter] has folded into the zeitgeist."

After the GTA 6 Extended Look premiered in August, people immediately spotted what they thought was Dexter's apartment building from the TV show. Now that GTA 6 has arrived, people found the apartment building in the game, and you can, too, by following GameSpot's Dexter apartment guide here.

On the TV show, Dexter dismembers his victims, stuffs them into garbage bags, and dumps them into the nearby harbor on his boat, the Slice of Life.

Players can also get into a kill house that bears a resemblance to the one that Dexter uses on the show, complete with plastic sheets for the blood splatter, hammers, and cleavers. Players have also found bones underwater, presumably another reference to Dexter.

#3596. 'Nocturne' Star Teases [Spoiler]'s Potential Death After 'Devastating' Twist

Chrissy Metz is speaking out on the latest twist on Nocturne that is hinting at a major death on the show.

During the Friday, November 20, episode of the Apple TV show, Jonah (Liev Schreiber) came to the realization that Jurek’s (Stephen Graham) kidnappings weren’t about the people who were taken. Instead, it was about hurting the people closest to them, who previously died by suicide as a result of the grief.

At the same time, Ida (Metz) — who was reunited with her son after his abduction — tried to decode a message Michael (Landon Valentin) was trying to give her from the person who took him. A chilling game of hangman led to Ida realizing the mystery word was her name — as the ominous hangman hinted that Ida would need to take her own life in order to get her daughter back as well.

“That’s what’s so petrifying about Jurek is that he doesn’t do the killing. The people do it to themselves,” Metz, 46, explained about the psychological warfare during an exclusive interview with Us. “It’s a lot.”

Metz called the reveal “beyond chilling and scary and sad and just devastating.”

“Nothing is really stronger than a mother’s love and I think that at that point she’s prepared to do whatever he asks of her and to keep her children safe,” she said about Us‘ concern for Ida moving forward. “I think you got that right.”

Nocturne follows a former homicide detective who relocates to a small Pennsylvania town, which comes under attack by an imprisoned serial killer. At the center of the case is Ida’s family, who is reeling from the return of her son — but also her daughter’s ongoing disappearance.

While Metz told Us she would love another season, she remained more tight-lipped about whether Ida could actually return, adding, “It was wonderful to work with everybody and they’re obviously so talented and it was really wonderful to watch a master class of actors. Should you be worried? Yes, I think you should be a little worried.”

She continued: “There’s some things that will transpire that I think will be shocking and I know for me it’s something that I’ve never done in any role before, which was concerning for Stephen [Graham] and Liev, who were like, ‘Are you sure?’ And I’m like, ‘This is not real.'”

Metz hinted that the story lines evolved.

“They were sort of campaigning for us to do something different but it is shocking. It’s scary,” she told Us. “It is very intense. Something very different.”

While reflecting on the role, Metz also discussed getting the chance to depict such a rich story.

“I always say that women aren’t depicted on screen enough. The stories are just not told enough. I’m so glad that they made her a woman [since she is a man in the book] and a mother. She is a regular woman just trying to survive as a single mom and I know that story very well because my mom was a single mom and raised children on her own,” she told Us. “I know what it’s like to sort of live paycheck to paycheck, and hope that you have enough for bills and to put food on the table. So I gravitate toward those those women and those characters and the stories because they don’t get told enough. I think people need to feel seen and heard in any way and that’s what’s brilliant about art and TV and film.”

Nocturne airs new episodes Fridays on Apple TV.

#3595. Dolly Parton on Her Mother Avie Lee Parton’s Album, Mama Sings

Many people know of my mama, Avie Lee Owens Parton, from my song “Coat of Many Colors,” but my mama gave me a gift that was far more valuable than a colorful coat. She gave me the gift of music.

As far back as I can remember, Mama loved to sing—at church, at family get-togethers, and most of all to her children. Her love of music came naturally; she had inherited it from her parents, her grandparents, and all the way back to Wales, where her family, the Owens, came from. Most of all, she inherited her love of music from her father, the Rev. Jake Owens. Grandpa Owens was a singer, songwriter, musician, and music teacher, in addition to being a full time Pentecostal preacher. He and my grandma Rena raised eight children, and all of them took to music in one way or another.

So, it was a natural thing that Mama shared her love of music with her children. She especially loved the old mountain songs—ballads that reached all the way back to the British Isles, popular songs from the 1800s that mountain people had made their own and, of course, beloved hymns.

So, when my uncle Louis Owens, Porter Wagoner, and I opened Fireside Recording Studio in Nashville in 1973, both my uncle Louis and I knew we had to get Mama in the recording studio to capture her songs on tape. Working with just a guitarist and an autoharp player, Mama recorded her own versions of some of her favorite songs.

Dolly Parton, Carl Butler, Avie Lee Parton, Robert Lee Parton, and Pearl Butler.

The plan was to release an album, but for one reason or another, it never happened. Fortunately, my uncle Louis saved all the tapes, and when he passed away, his son Richie, who has always loved our family history and heritage, decided to clean them up and get them released.

Dolly Parton and her mother, Avie Lee Parton.

Many of them are well-known tunes, but you may know them under different titles. Like all mountain singers, Mama preferred to call songs by the name she’d learned them under, and we decided that that was the way we needed to present them to you.

If you’ve ever wondered where my music came from, this album tells the story, and I am so proud, happy, and honored to have shared this music and my mama’s voice with you.

#3594. GTA 6 Players Captivated By Mandy Apparently Include A Former Nintendo President

A character named Mandy has the attention of many Grand Theft Auto 6 players--and that appears to include Reggie Fils-Aimé, the man who used to run Nintendo of America.

Per GamesRadar, former Nintendo marketing and public relations manager Krysta Yang joked on social media that GTA 6, which is front-loaded with a lot of simulation-like busywork in the first chapter, is "adult Animal Crossing," posting images that highlight parallels between GTA 6 and Animal Crossing: New Horizons. Fils-Aimé quoted the post, saying: "If so, where's Mandy?"

It's slightly eyebrow raising that the former executive for a family-friendly company like Nintendo seems to have a strong opinion for a rather promiscuous video game character. No judgment to Fils-Aimé, of course, but talk around Mandy carries a certain... tone. Minor spoilers for the early parts of GTA 6 follow.

One of the earliest missions in GTA 6 has Jason stopping by Mandy's home to collect rent. Long story short, she flirts pretty aggressively with Jason, who clearly isn't reciprocating, and Mandy doesn't take it well. And no, even if players wanted to, you can't romance Mandy.

It doesn't help that it's implied that Mandy carries a dark secret, with Jason discovering a severed finger while fixing her sink's pipes. I'm not sure if anyone in Animal Crossing is that shady.

So what does this post say about Reggie Fils-Aimé as a person? It's unclear what he thinks of the character--all we know is that he'd really like to know who the Animal Crossing equivalent of Mandy would be. It certainly wouldn't be Isabelle, so take your pick of any weird villagers you've encountered. Either way, it seems that Fils-Aimé is playing GTA 6 like the rest of us or, at the very least, is in tune with the massive cultural zeitgeist the game has produced.

#3593. How to Check Your Flight Status After the FAA Canceled the Ground Stop for All Airports

Update, 8:41 p.m.: The Federal Aviation Administration announced it has ended the ground stop.

On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States. If you're planning to fly this afternoon or evening, or you have friends or family doing the same, you're likely concerned about tracking flight statuses. While there's still a lot we don't know, there are tools to help track flights at this time:

There are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not. If you have the flight number, the fastest method is to Google it: Google will display a live tracker of your flight at the top of the results page. You can also head to the airline's official website to track your flight: United Airlines, for example, has a flight tracker where you can either enter your route information or your flight number. Most, if not all, airlines will have a similar tool you can use.

Alternatively, you can use a site or service that tracks all flights. FlightAware is one such site and has a flight tracker that lets you search flights—so long as you know the origin and the destination. If you have the flight number, your iPhone can help: You can enter your flight number into Spotlight search to see a live tracker, or you can text a contact your flight number, then tap the link that appears under the number to see a tracker of the flight.

At this time, the exact reason isn't totally clear. According to the agency, “The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” but the FAA hasn't said what caused those communications issues or when they expect to lift the grounding. The grounding order comes one day after a massive Microsoft outage that disrupted service for users of Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products. It also comes one day after Ars Technica reported that the FAA was rolling out an AI-powered tool to help manage air traffic across the country.

This is only the third time in U.S. history that the FAA has made such an order—once after 9/11, and again in January of 2023 due to a pilot alert system issue; the latter ground stop lasted around 90 minutes.

I expected a road trip comedy and got so much more.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Amid the various kinds of films I enjoy, coming-of-age movies hold a special place in my heart. There’s something special about a story that sees young people navigating growing pains, whether they be Black-led coming-of-age stories or those told from other perspectives. On that note, I had been meaning to watch the much revered Smoke Signals for some time, and I finally did that amid Native American Heritage Month. I’m pleased to say that not only is the movie great as promised, but it also surprised me in two ways.

Released in 1998, Smoke Signals is based on screenwriter Sherman Alexie’s The Lone Ranger and Tonto Fistfight in Heaven. The Chris Eyre-directed road trip dramedy primarily centers around two Indigenous teens – Victor Joseph (Adam Beach) and Thomas Builds-the-Fire (Evan Adams). The mismatched pair set off on a trip from their Idaho-based reservation to Phoenix, Arizona, to collect the ashes of Victor’s recently deceased father.

It’s an excellent film that offers its share of funny and sweet moments, but what I didn’t expect was for the movie to get so dark at times. While I knew the general premise going in, I didn’t realize Victor’s relationship with his parents, specifically with his dad, would be used to highlight such serious subject matter. For instance, something that’s established early on is that Victor’s father, Arnold (played brilliantly by Gary Farmer), abandoned him and his mother years prior, which is a fact that fuels Victor’s resentment towards him.

Alcoholism is also explored in great depth, as flashbacks show both of the Arnolds dealing with it, to the point where a young Victor destroys their beer in defiance. It’s a striking moment and serves as the wake-up call Victor’s mother, Arlene (Tantoo Cardinal), needs. Additionally, domestic abuse is a key theme, as Arnold is shown abusing Victor and Arlene on different occasions. Overall, through the Josephs, audiences get a nuanced look at dysfunctional intergenerational relationships.

Smoke Signals also has other grim moments. I mean, the film opens with a flashback to the night of a Fourth of July party, at which point Thomas’ parents are killed in a house fire. And the only reason baby Thomas survives is due to being saved by Arnold, who Thomas grows to idolize despite his faults. While the darker material caught me off guard, I truly appreciated Eyre and Alexie tackling such subject matter and doing so with some layered Indigenous characters.

Throughout the film, there’s also a heavy emphasis on the Native American tradition of oral storytelling. Much of that is thanks to Thomas, who tells stories – that vary in terms of how true they are – whether people want to hear them or not. Adams delivers these soliloquies perfectly, and they add a soulful element to the film. I particularly love when Thomas bonds over storytelling with Arnold’s Phoenix- based friend, Suzy Song (Irene Bedard), who is a badass Indigenous woman in a fairly understated way.

All in all, this keen focus on storytelling only enhances the movie, and Eyre and Alexie’s reverence for it is more than evident. It also opens the door for viewers like myself to gain a better understanding of an aspect of Native American culture we wouldn’t otherwise be privy to. As a viewer, I really enjoy being engulfed in different cultural perspectives via film and TV, and truly relish whenever nuanced stories centered on (and told by) Indigenous people are pushed to the forefront.

I can’t recommend Smoke Signals enough and, in many ways, it feels like a precursor to one of my favorite shows, Reservation Dogs (which is streamable with a Hulu subscription). So check out the movie now, as it’s available to stream with a Paramount+ subscription.

#3591. Jonathan Rinderknecht Found Guilty of Starting Devastating 2025 Palisades Fire

Jonathan Rinderknecht has been found guilty of starting the devastating 2025 Palisades Fire, which killed 12 people and destroyed entire neighborhoods across Los Angeles and Malibu.

According to multiple reports, jurors convicted former Uber driver Rinderknecht, 30, of igniting a fire on January 1, 2025, that smoldered undetected beneath root systems before reigniting days later on January 7.

The blaze, which became known as the Palisades Fire, tore through the region, leaving widespread devastation and claiming 12 lives. The inferno was one of the most destructive wildfires in California history.

Rinderknecht pleaded not guilty to federal charges of destruction of property by means of fire and arson.

The first charge was narrowed to focus on the January 1 blaze, known as the Lachman Fire, while the second related to the Palisades Fire itself. He was ultimately convicted on both counts.

The Palisades fire verdict comes after prosecutors pursued a retrial following a deadlocked jury in Rinderknecht’s first trial in June. That jury reportedly voted 10-2 in favor of acquittal after two weeks of proceedings, prompting prosecutors to continue building their case.

A third charge of timber set afire was later dropped when a new indictment was filed ahead of the retrial.

During the second trial, prosecutors presented a more streamlined case, relying on digital forensic evidence, expert testimony and details about Rinderknecht’s state of mind in the hours before the fire. As they sought to establish Rinderknecht as the Palisades Fire starter, they emphasized the evidence surrounding the fires and his actions and put less focus on his alleged resentment toward wealthy and powerful people than they previously did.

In October 2025, authorities publicly announced they had arrested a Palisades Fire suspect.

“Today we are announcing the arrest of 29-year-old Jonathan Rinderknecht on a criminal complaint charging him with maliciously starting what became the Palisades Fire in January,” Bill Essayli, acting U.S. Attorney for the Central District of California, wrote via X on October 8, 2025.

“The complaint alleges that Rinderknecht started a fire in Pacific Palisades on New Year’s Day — a blaze that eventually turned into one of the most destructive fires in Los Angeles history, causing death and widespread destruction.”

The Palisades Fire burned more than 23,000 acres of land in communities in and around Los Angeles, including Pacific Palisades, Malibu and the Santa Monica mountains. It was fully contained on January 31.

#3590. Cheeky Malware Linked To Popular Gacha Game Cracks City Security

East Asia--and particularly Japan--has been suffering a rash of cybersecurity incidents as of late, affecting everything from major banks and cellphone service providers to city governments and small businesses. Gaming has been one of many areas targeted: between arcade games on Sega's network going offline, 11 million Capcom IDs being compromised, and a high-schooler hacking Bandai-Namco, some major publishers have been suffering a string of embarrassments.

One recent incident involved the PC launcher for the popular gacha action shooter NIKKE: Goddess of Victory, where malicious code would install a trojan called k2f that would compromise an individual's PC, taking screenshots, logging inputs, and installing/executing programs. Unfortunately for one Japanese municipality, someone's gacha habits may have lead to a much bigger incident.

Iwamizawa is a city of about 75,000 located in Hokkaido, Japan's northernmost island. It's not a place that makes a lot of news, but it recently went viral on the Japanese-speaking side of social media. As reported by Automaton, the city issued a notice that an IT sub-sub-contractor handling the city's fixed asset records suffered a security breach--specifically, a k2f hijack. Observers soon surmised that the most likely source of k2f would be someone playing a certain sexy gacha game on a work PC.

The subcontractor in question, IT services company GIS Hokkaido, would then confirm to Japanese tech news site ITMedia that, yes, NIKKE's compromised PC launcher was the source of the problem. When asked if an employee or subcontractor had launched the game on a work PC, GIS politely replied that "they would prefer not to comment."

Moral of the story? While there's nothing wrong with playing a suggestive gacha game on your own time, you probably shouldn't do it on the clock, and definitely not on a company PC, lest you become internet meme fodder.

#3589. Want to Smell Bisexual? A Hit Podcast Has the Perfume for You

You Must Remember This is a podcast dedicated, as its host Karina Longworth says in every intro, to exploring the secret and/or forgotten histories of Hollywood’s first century. Longworth, who is an LA–based writer and film preservationist, usually tells her stories in themed seasons. Those include Erotic 90’s, spanning the introduction of the NC-17 rating to Eyes Wide Shut; Dead Blondes (Marilyn Monroe, Jean Harlow, Veronica Lake); and a whole series exploring the web of connections Charles Manson had to Hollywood. It’s addictive, exhaustively researched, and narrated in a way that is both soothing and trancelike.

Longworth is a native Angeleno who has been writing about film for years. She was a film editor and critic at the LA Weekly for three years until 2012; wrote books on Al Pacino and Meryl Streep; and then started You Must Remember This is 2014. She’s also part of a film-loving couple: her husband of 8 years is the Knives Out writer and director Rian Johnson.

The latest season of the podcast is called The Bisexuals, spotlighting the stories of actors and actresses whose love lives were often much more diverse than anything sanctioned by a studio. One star that the season discusses is Libby Holman, a singer and socialite who married the tobacco heir Zachary Smith Reynolds in 1931. Not only did she have a fruitful sex life with Tallulah Bankhead and Montgomery Clift, but she was known for her signature scent called Jungle Gardenia.

In honor of that bombastic perfume that wafted off of her, Longworth, 46, collaborated with Joey Rosin, who formulated a fragrance, Bisexual. Vanity Fair spoke to Longworth about moviegoing in Los Angeles versus New York, what she smelled like as a teenager, being in grad school in your 40s, and her thoughts about Quentin Tarantino’s film programming.

The interview that follows has been condensed for length and clarity.

Vanity Fair: What was the first perfume you remember wearing?

Karina Longworth: Opium by YSL was really a big deal for me when I was 18, 19. It was one of the first perfumes that I ever knew about. I started with The Body Shop’s Tea Rose oil. I didn’t really have any female adult influences because my mom died when I was 11, and so I had to sort of figure out that whole world.

Have you always wanted to make a perfume? Are you a perfume nerd?

So I never had an ambition to make a perfume, but over the past 10 years, I’ve become really into perfume. I used to rent an office space in the same building as an independent perfumer, Jacqueline Ella Steele, whose brand was called Goest— which doesn’t exist anymore—but she made a perfume called Silent Films. She was the first person I contacted about trying to formulate this perfume. But she’s out of business. So that’s when I started asking around and I got led to Joey Rosin.

I got the idea because, in reading and writing about Libby Holman, there are all these anecdotes of her walking into a room in a cloud of Jungle Gardenia, to the point where, people who were attracted to her were attracted to it, and people who didn’t like her found it so disgusting. I thought there was something really interesting about that, how the same scent could be either attractive or repellent, depending on how you felt about the person wearing it.

What does a bisexual smell like? In this case jungles and gardenia

Personalities, voices and clothes all depend on who’s doing it.

There’s this really incredible anecdote in Patricia Bosworth’s Montgomery Clift biography about how one of Montgomery Clift’s friends was at a party at Treetops, Libby Holman’s estate, and she was looking for the bathroom, and accidentally walked into her bedroom, and the bed was a tangle of white satin sheets, and there’s a giant bottle of barbiturates on the nightstand and everything just reeked of Jungle Gardenia. She was grossed out, but then she also got the impression this is Libby and Monty’s sex lair.

We didn’t try to copy the exact old fragrance. Joey does his research, and he did research into what the original notes were. But we talked about not wanting it to be a slavish copy, and instead just trying to evoke for both of us what jungle would smell like with gardenia, and how that could evoke Libby’s story. And so we played around with adding different types of smoke to it.

I’ve been to Tahiti. I’m trying to think if I’ve ever been to a jungle. We talked a lot about tropical plants and what the dirt would smell like, and the heat. It’s like hot weather almost has a smell. But then pairing that with this kind of old lady scent of gardenia. I went to visit his studio in Brooklyn a few times and he mailed some samples to me in Los Angeles. And by that point, it was like four iterations that were almost exactly the same. So it was just about what was giving me the best vibe.

I was living alone in Rochester, N.Y. in a depressing situation because of the weather and being very alone, having no social life.

But you loved your grad school program, right? I forget the name but I know it’s long.

L. Jeffrey Selznick School of Film Preservation at the George Eastman Museum. I got so much out of the program, but it was grueling, physically, and mentally, and emotionally. It was really difficult to suddenly be living alone in a place where I felt like I had no one I could really talk to.

So you were in an entirely new, but temporary situation.

I started relying on scented candles to improve my mood and to change my mood. If I got home feeling terrible, the fragrance was helpful. I also had nowhere to wear perfume. At first I thought I would just make a candle, and then as I started learning more about fragrance, I learned that candles have to go through a much more rigorous process. And it takes a lot longer. We were not going to be able to get it done in time to have a presale like we have during the podcast season. But in the future, I would like to do a signature scent for You Must Remember This and have it available as a perfume and a candle.

It would be classic, but in a different way. I’m very inspired by the signature scent that they have at the Chateau [Marmont].

There has been a lot of talk about moviegoing being back. How has your tour been?

It has been great. In Savannah they sold 400 tickets to a very obscure, pre-code movie on a Friday night.

People must ask you a lot of podcast questions. What are your tips?

I say I don’t know what form yours is going to take, but mine takes the form of writing an extremely detailed script, and then sitting by myself in a room and reading it into a microphone.

I built a recording studio. I bought a little house in Laurel Canyon at the end of a private road, like at the end of a cul-de-sac, but you feel like you’re in the middle of the forest. I bought it from this woman who had lived there for 15 years and was kind of an all-purpose healer. She basically built a soundproof room with clay on the walls and crystals embedded into the clay, where she would do sound baths with them. When I saw this house, it was just perfect.

Which city has a better movie scene, New York or LA?

New York’s way better than LA, but LA is getting better.

Did someone buy the Vista? I loved that theater.

[Quentin] Tarantino owns the Vista. Because it’s Tarantino, he won’t let them show anything digital. It has to be a film print, and so he’ll show a new movie if there’s a print, like The Odyssey played there, Sinners played there. But when there isn’t a new movie out that is on a print, he programs whatever he wants to see. He also does a lot of like Saturday morning matinees of classical Hollywood cinema that is just his taste, you know. Sometimes it’s my taste, sometimes it’s not. It’s a lot of Jerry Lewis. But one thing I will say for Tarantino is that when he discovers a filmmaker or genre or something from the past, he shows. He’s been showing all these William Beaudine silent films, and I think that’s great because silent film has really fallen out of fashion in LA.

I was leaving to interview you today and someone said, “Oh, I love that podcast,” and was talking about the Manson series. Is that your most popular?

It changes. Increasingly, people are asking about the Polly Platt series.

Do you know what the next series is going to be?

I have two ideas that would involve talking to people or family members of subjects who have passed away, but who could give me access to sort of the family lore. I am in contact with both of those families, but I need to kind of do the legwork, talking to them more and figure out which story makes the most sense. I also sketched out a very long season about the three stars of Rebel Without a Cause. That is something that people have been asking me to do for years. But the thing that stops me from doing it is that we still don’t know exactly what happened to Natalie Wood. But that’s kind of in my back pocket.

#3588. Sarah Michelle Gellar and Freddie Prinze Jr. Find ‘Crazy’ Family Connection

Sarah Michelle Gellar and her husband Freddie Prinze Jr. have more in common than they they bargained for

Speaking to E! News on Friday, November 21, Gellar, 49, revealed the couple recently uncovered a surprising family connection through Ancestry that has them rethinking just how small the world really is.

“We always joke that the closest connection I had to my husband’s side of the family was that for a small time I went to the same high school that my husband’s dad went to, and that was, like, sort of our one thing,” the Buffy the Vampire Slayer alum told the outlet.

She continued, “Then through Ancestry, we found out that our grandparents lived less than two miles away from each other in the Bronx at one point, which they could have potentially known each other. That’s kind of crazy.”

Although Gellar is a New York native, Prinze Jr., 49, was born in Los Angeles and raised in New Mexico. His late father, comedian Freddie Prinze, was originally from New York, making the family connection even more surprising.

The couple first met while filming 1997’s I Know What You Did Last Summer, but their romance wasn’t immediate. Instead, their relationship began with a series of road trips that ultimately sparked a friendship.

“She didn’t have a driver’s license. She didn’t know how to drive,” Prinze Jr. exclusively told Us in April 2020, recalling how they first connected.

“We were shooting in Southport, North Carolina, which was an hour’s drive from Wilmington, which was the biggest city that was closest to us. … So, I started driving her, and that’s when her and I became friends,” he explained.

The She’s All That actor said the pair would talk about “life” and their “completely different philosophies on just about everything.”

“By the end of the movie, I just wanted to be friends with her because I thought she was too skinny and I wanted to cook for her. Because that’s what my family does,” Prinze Jr. recalled.

He added, “And so, we started this weekly barbecue thing at her house, and me and my cousins would come over and cook food for her and her friends. And then we’d make sure everybody ate, and that was kind of how our friendship began.”

That friendship eventually turned into a romance, with Gellar and Prinze Jr. tying the knot in 2002. The pair welcomed daughter Charlotte in 2009, followed by son Rocky in 2012.

Over the years, the couple have also reunited onscreen several times, including in Scooby-Doo in 2002 and its sequel, Scooby-Doo 2: Monsters Unleashed, in 2004. Gellar also made a brief cameo in Prinze Jr.’s 1999 rom-com She’s All That, while the pair appeared in separate cameos  in Clerks III in 2022.

#3587. The Surprising History of the Royal Walkabout

“I have to be seen to be believed,” the late Queen Elizabeth II once said. And on Christmas Day, the royal family will be seen en masse during their annual walkabout on their way to services at St. Mary Magdalene Church on the Sandringham estate. For years, the holiday stroll, which features major and minor royals mingling with the public, has been a milestone event on the royal calendar.

But three controversial royals, the former Prince Andrew, Prince Harry and Meghan Markle, Duchess of Sussex, almost certainly will not be there. While Andrew has disappeared into his new life at Marsh Farm in Norfolk, Harry and Meghan have continued the tradition of the walkabout, reportedly infuriating the palace with a planned meet-and-greet with a small group of well-wishers in Nottingham. Although no longer working members of the royal family, it seems the couple knows the value and the power of this famous tradition, whose origins are far more recent than many believe.

For centuries, commoners were lucky to get a glimpse of royals riding a horse on a march across the country or nodding from a carriage on the way to the opening of parliament. The first Buckingham Palace balcony appearance was not until 1851, when Prince Albert came upon the idea of Queen Victoria appearing to celebrate the Great Exhibition of London.

The leading figure behind the idea of making the monarchy more visible to the public was a surprising one: the dour, but savvy George V, who ascended the throne in 1910. “I may be uninspiring,” he admitted, “but I’m damned if I’m an alien.”

Queen Elizabeth II and Prince William waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace during Trooping the Colour on June 16, 1990. Pictured: Prince Edward, Duchess Of York, Queen Mother, Princess Margaret, Queen Elizabeth II, Prince Philip, Prince William, The Grand Duchess Josephine Charlotte Of Luxembourg, Prince Harry, Prince Charles, Lord Frederick Windsor, Princess Diana and Lady Rose Windsor.

These royal appearances ramped up significantly during the first World War, when the royal family came under scrutiny for their German lineage. George visited everyday soldiers on the Front, and Queen Mary and her children spent hours visiting the wounded in hospitals.

“George took ‘getting out and about’ to new levels. He visited industrial areas and poor housing, went down a coal mine and went on a relentless round of opening hospitals and inspecting regiments,” royal news website Royal Central notes. “Queen Mary once retorted to a princess complaining about yet another hospital visit: ‘We are the royal family—and we love hospitals.’”

However, these events were still carefully curated, with a distance maintained between the royal family and those they were visiting. It was not until 1939, that the first unofficial walkabout occurred, when King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (better known as the Queen Mother) went to tour Canada on a goodwill tour in the midst of the looming war. In May, the couple laid a wreath at Ottawa National War Memorial while an estimated 10,000 veterans looked on.

Overcome with emotion, the royal couple decided to go into the crowd to speak with onlookers. A CBC radio journalist watching the scene could hardly have sounded more in awe. “They all look most happy, most excited,” the reporter said. “One had the hand of the queen in one hand and the hand of the king in another. A delighted expression.”

George and Elizabeth were equally touched, and continued these meet-and-greets throughout the tour. “I lost my heart to Canada and to Canadians, and my feelings have not changed with the passage of time,” the Queen Mother recalled.

Known for her effusive personality and warmth, the Queen Mother became a pro at speaking with everyday subjects. During World War II, George and Elizabeth were praised for going among the people in bombed out areas devastated by the Blitz, listening to their woes and offering encouragement and strength.

Queen Elizabeth II on walkabout in Launceston, Tasmania, during her tour of Australia, 1970.

But it was not until Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip toured Australia and New Zealand in 1970 that the modern walkabout was truly introduced into the British royal calendar. There are different origin stories about how the modern walkabout came to be. One version asserts that it was a spontaneous decision of the Queen to walk to her next stop in order to chat, shake hands and accept flowers from schoolchildren in New Zealand.

Others say that first walk was the brainchild of the modernizing Australian courtier William Heseltine, known as the “mastermind behind the monarchy.” A firm believer in making the family seem more approachable and normal, he was also behind the 1969 Royal Family documentary. But if that project proved to be controversial, the walkabout (a term coined as a result of the tour) was a smash hit.

According to Kitty Kelley, the first royal walkabout did not occur in London until 1972, during the celebration of Elizabeth and Philip’s 25th wedding anniversary. “People were agog; their sovereign had never been known to speak to ordinary people,” Kelley writes in The Royals. “This was the first royal walkabout London had ever seen, and flag-waving Britons cheered as the Queen, the Duke of Edinburgh, Prince Charles, and Princess Anne melted into the crowd, greeting people and trying to make the royal family appear less remote.”

While the Queen reportedly enjoyed the intimacy of the walkabout, not every royal family member was quite as thrilled. “At nineteen years old suddenly being dropped in the middle of the street, suddenly being told to pick someone and talk to them,” Princess Anne said. “Fun? No, I don’t think so. A challenge.”

Queen Elizabeth II visits the Town Hall in Sydney with Emmet McDermott, Lord Mayor of Sydney, during her tour of Australia, May 1970.

Soon, the walkabout was a major part of every royal’s schedule, and family members had to learn how to do them—like it or not. “I learnt the way a monkey learns—by watching its parents,” King Charles once said.

During international tours, the walkabouts made a packed schedule even more tiring, but Queen Elizabeth II never faltered. “On a tour of Canada, visiting Saskatchewan, the Canadian minister Alvin Hamilton was concerned that the Queen had been on her feet all day and had not even requested a ‘health break,’” Karen Dolby writes in The Wicked Wit of Queen Elizabeth II. “Her private secretary breezily replied that the Minister for Northern Affairs and National Resources need not worry, ‘Her Majesty is trained for eight hours.’ It’s impossible not to wonder about the training sessions.”

She also leaned upon her sense of humor when meeting folks of all different stripes. “On a walkabout in Scotland, a helpful observer commented that she looked just like the Queen, to which she quickly replied, ‘How reassuring,’” Dolby notes.

According to Dolby, the Queen also developed a system to communicate with her staff while talking with the public. If things were going well, she held her handbag in the crook of her left arm. If she wanted someone to relieve her so she could move on, the handbag was dropped to her side.

But the person who truly transformed the modern walkabout was Princess Diana, much to her husband Prince Charles’s chagrin. “Charles was smart enough to see what a stunning political asset Diana had become—but he was also deeply disturbed by all the adoration coming his young wife’s way,” Tina Brown writes in The Diana Chronicles.

From the start it was clear the young Princess had a connection with everyday people unlike any other royal. During a walkabout while touring Wales in 1981, Charles joked, “I seem to do nothing but collect flowers these days, I know my role.”

As Dianamania swept the world, the Princess became more and more comfortable with connecting with her often-rabid fans. Far from a stiff gloved handshake, she would clasp hands gloveless, hug well-wishers, kneel to speak with children. Frustrated that Diana constantly pulled focus, Charles delivered pithy one-liners with a forced smile. At one walkabout, the crowd openly groaned when they realized Charles was coming to their side, not Diana. “It’s not fair is it?” Charles quipped to the crowd. “You’d better ask for your money back.”

But despite Charles’s jealousy, he could not deny the impact Diana had during these walkabouts. “Everyone was really buoyed up to see her and she was making an effort to go along and speak to people and people appreciated the effort she put into meeting them,” one person she spoke with remembered. “I know it was her job but she gave that little bit extra to people that made her different and stand out.”

“She made people happy,” he noted. “It’s a rare gift.”

Catherine, Princess of Wales, has followed in her mother-in-law’s footsteps as a walkabout all-star. According to historian Robert Jobson, Catherine was initially scared during the walkabout, offering up the stiff refrain, “Thank you so much. We are so delighted to be here,” over and over. But she quickly acclimated and has become known for her chatty and warm ways. “There’s a real art to walkabouts,” she has said. “Everybody teases me in the family that I spend far too long chatting. I still have to learn a little bit more, and to pick up a few more tips, I suppose.”

In fact, it has become a sport for the press to catch Prince William subtly attempting to move Catherine along, often eventually giving up. During the Christmas Day walkabout in 2024, she was the last royal to leave the receiving line, quipping “I think I’ve lost my family!”

According to royal author Robert Hardman, King Charles can also be unusually chatty. No one quite wants to go up and go, ‘Sir, can you get a move on?’ he says. “Instead, Queen Camilla will nudge him in the small of his back with the corner of her handbag.”

But the predilection is one Camilla shares as well. On a walkabout in Wrexham, an irritated Charles was overheard telling an aide “Can we try to get [Camilla] back again? Please? We need to go! I was trying to wait for her, but she goes on!”

Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, attend University of the South Pacific on October 24, 2018 in Suva, Fiji.

Learning the art of the walkabout—what to say, what not to say—is a lesson every royal must figure out, often on the job. When Meghan Markle married Prince Harry in 2018, she admitted her ignorance. “I never saw pictures or videos of a walkabout,” she claimed.

And with the advent of cell phones, the job has become much more difficult. “I’m glad that I’m not starting now because at least you had people to talk to. Now you don’t really. Phones are bad enough, but the iPads—you can’t even see their heads,” Princess Anne said.

And these engagements can occasionally go south. In 2018, the Duchess of Sussex was rushed out of a market in Fiji after the walkabout got out of hand. There are also the occasional overzealous fans, including recently when a woman attempted to kiss Prince William on the cheek. And who can forget the supremely uncomfortable walkabout at Windsor after the Queen’s death in 2022, when a warring William, Catherine, Harry and Meghan greeted public mourners. It was, Catherine reportedly said, “one of the hardest things she’d ever had to do.”

Walkabouts are also a logistical headache for royal protection officers. “You are always aware of who is in the crowd,” former royal bodyguard Simon Morgan explained to Hello! “That is one of the positives of our royal family, they always want to go and meet people and as a protection officer, you have to accept what their wishes are. The current trend of hugs, high fives and selfies, that’s going to continue, so the protection officer’s job is really brought to the front then, because the protection officer is constantly looking for what could go wrong, you are constantly working things through your mind for the ‘what if, what if, what if.’

But the walkabout shows no sign of disappearing anytime soon. And come Christmas Day, there will be cheers, hugs, and an enormous amount of quick, polite chats about the weather that citizens who wait and brave the winter cold will never forget.

Now, The Simpsons may get all the credit for "accurately" predicting news events, but it’s time we give a shout-out to one of the best sitcoms of all time: Friends. That's because decades after a funny interaction about Batman and James Bond happened on that show, The Batman star, Robert Pattinson, was cast as 007. Seriously, I really can’t get over the fact that Monica and Chandler debated this decades before he was cast as both.

In the debate, the couple was arguing about which icon was cooler, and it's really never been more relevant than it is right now. At present, Robert Pattinson is DC's Bruce Wayne, and he is currently filming The Batman: Part II, which is reportedly slated for a 2028 release. He also just got announced as the next James Bond. So, in reaction to all this, HBO Max resurrected this Friends moment:

The humorous moment occurred in Season 7, Episode 20, “The One with Rachel’s Big Kiss,” and is thanks to Rachel, who hooked Chandler and Ross up with celebrity tuxes for Chandler’s wedding to Monica. However, after our favorite funny man discovers his soon-to-be brother-in-law is wearing a tux worn by Val Kilmer, he fears his Pierce Brosnan tux is no longer the coolest one. This led to Monica trying to convince Chandler that 007 was cooler, which is the scene you witnessed above.

At this point, I’ve seen a plethora of Pattinson in every franchise jokes, but this one may just be my favorite. Though those who are predicting he’ll appear in Doomsday to stop Doctor Doom or pop up in The Hunger Games tie for second place. Regardless, fans continue to have BIG reactions to the 007 news, which has yet to die down on the internet. So naturally, they had to weigh in on the Friends debate too, and some even had to call out his Twilight days:

Personally, I think we should dub Pattinson ‘Batbond’ and call it a day.

Along with the funny reactions to this Friends debate, some fan reactions had me emotional, with reminders that Matthew Perry was an avid Batman fan. He even collected memorabilia, which, to me, throws a point in Batman’s favor and adds another Friends episode to the list of Perry's work that will forever make me miss the actor.

Now, getting back to this clip from Friends, I think this Batman vs. Bond debate may live on longer than Pattinson’s tracksuit meme. Though something tells me the actor won’t mind.

However, it’ll be a bit before we see him return to the cape or put on a suit. Don’t worry, though, we aren’t going to experience a Pattinson drought. The actor can be seen in Dune: Part Three as Scytale, when it premieres on the 2026 movie schedule on December 18.

Then, the 26th movie in the spy franchise is expected to start production next year, and work on The Batman: Part II will continue. Personally, I think it'd be kind of cool if they brought the Friends debate full circle by dropping the movies at the same time for a ‘Batbond’ double feature event.

#3585. Melania Trump Reveals Advice She Gave Son Barron About Dating Scene

Melania Trump has a few tips for her son, Barron Trump, as he navigates his dating life.

Melania, who shares Barron, 20, with her husband, President Donald Trump, recalled the advice she provided her son in the Friday, November 20 episode of her new Prime Video docuseries, MELANIA.

“I always say it’s a dangerous world out there,” Melania, 56, said in the docuseries, adding, “and be careful.”

While Melania may have some words of wisdom when it comes to dating, she emphasized that Barron can always turn to her for advice on anything, not just romance.

“I will always be there for him,” she said. “We have very open communication regarding life. I will always be there for him. I am, and I will always be. And he knows that he’s my priority, and he will always be my priority.”

The former model also joked about her parenting style, declaring, “I’m a very cool mom to Barron, and I remind him all the time.”

When asked whether Barron has any intentions of following in his father’s political footsteps, Melania said it was his call.

“I think it’s very important that he lives the life that he wants and what makes him happy. I don’t like to be controlling over him. He has his own mind, his own character, his own beliefs, and I respect that,” she said.

The First Lady added, “He likes politics. He gave his father incredible advice. He told him how to connect with the young voters, his generation. Told him who he needs to talk to. He introduced him to podcasts, to streamers.”

During a January appearance on Fox Business’ Mornings With Maria, Melania again noted that her son’s wellbeing was of the utmost importance to her.

“You need to be there for a child nonstop, especially when they need you, especially at that age that Barron is,” she said.

Melania has previously spoken about the importance of having a strong support system while raising her son. She was particularly grateful to have her late mother, Amalija Knavs, by her side throughout Barron’s childhood. Amalija died in 2024.

“My mother was the epitome of love and warmth, and for Barron, a grandmother who filled every moment with joy and wisdom,” Melania told USA Today in May. “Every story she read to Barron sparked his imagination, and every game they played strengthened their bond.”

#3584. Kate Middleton Wore Matching Amethyst Necklace and Earrings for Her First Engagement in India

The Princess of Wales touched down in India this Monday for a whirlwind three-day visit to the country with her husband, Prince William.

The couple visited Mumbai for the sixth Earthshot Prize Summit, which took place on Tuesday. It marked the Waleses’ first joint overseas visit since Catherine’s cancer diagnosis.

The busy schedule of engagements kicked off with a game of gully cricket—an informal version of the game played on the street. For the occasion, the Princess of Wales struck a balance between polished and casual, opting for crisp white Alexander McQueen trousers, paired with a white top layered under a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard.

The Princess of Wales debuted a pistachio blazer by Veronica Beard for the outing

The finishing touch? A matching set of green amethyst earrings and a drop necklace from one of Catherine’s favorite jewelry labels, Kiki McDonough. Catherine has at least 20 pairs of earrings from the jeweler, ranging from the blue topaz drops she wore to Royal Ascot to the green tourmaline, green amethyst and diamond earrings set in gold, designed specially for her to mark Princess Charlotte’s birth.

The apple green amethysts, which she wore in Mumbai, are among the lesser-seen designs in her collection but proved the perfect accessory for this first engagement.

While in Mumbai, the prince’s program focused on The Earthshot Prize and its mission to accelerate solutions to the world’s most pressing environmental challenges. The princess joined the prince for a number of engagements during the visit.

The Prince and Princess of Wales in Mumbai on Monday

During their time in Mumbai, the prince and princess also celebrated several of the deep cultural connections between the United Kingdom and India: cricket, fashion, and cinema.

Beginning with an engagement focused on the uniquely Indian passion of gully cricket andconcluding with a visit to the heart of Mumbai’s film industry, their royal highnessescelebrated the creativity, talent, and cultural influence that continue to shape modern India andstrengthen ties between the two countries.

The highlight of the visit was the Earthshot Prize ceremony on Tuesday, November 17. Five Earthshot leaders were given 1 million euros (about $1.1 million USD) to accelerate the impact of their innovative solutions. Mumbai made perfect sense as the host city; India is home to more Earthshot Prize winners and finalists than any other country.

The Princess of Wales looked elegant in a lime green blazer layered over an all-white ensemble

Since founding the prize in 2020, Prince William has attended all of the awards ceremonies: in London, Boston, Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro. Catherine joined the prince in London in 2021 and again in Boston the following year, but has missed recent editions in the further corners of the globe. This was partly due to the princess’s restricted work schedule while she underwent treatment for cancer and spent time in recovery.

It marked a return to the country for Prince William and Kate, who carried out a state visit in April 2016. The week-long tour saw the then Duke and Duchess of Cambridge explore Mumbai, New Delhi, Assam, and Bhutan, racking up a total of 22 engagements that saw them try their hand at cricket, meet Bollywood stars and royalty, and champion charitable causes close to their hearts.

It was one of four overseas trips taken by the couple that year. Although William and Kate still travel, it is with far less frequency as the couple prioritizes a stable family life. Their last major overseas tour was to the Caribbean in 2022.

Keep in mind that it doesn't add rear speakers, so you're still working with a 3.1 setup and sound that stays in front of you.

Amazon Fire TV Soundbar Plus with Subwoofer and Surround Sound Speakers is $349.99, down from $489.99. This is the complete 5.1 package, adding two rear speakers to the 3.1 bar and wireless subwoofer, so action scenes and other surround effects come from behind you, rather than only from the direction of the TV—but it costs $120 more than the discounted soundbar and subwoofer bundle, so it’s worth considering how much you want that surround-sound effect. Also, while the rear speakers connect to the soundbar wirelessly, each still needs a power outlet.

In short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Yes, Amazon has Black Friday sales, and we vet our deals to make sure they’re the best ones. You can also refer to guides like our live blog that have already done all of the vetting for you. And if you have an Amazon Prime membership, make the most of it.

No. If you find the product you're looking for with a major discount right now, get it. It's not likely to drop any lower, but it could always run out of stock. Take advantage of price matching or guarantees instead of waiting. Remember, you can always return products later if you change your mind. For the majority of products, the deal from Black Friday will be the same one on Cyber Monday.

#3582. Why Proserpina Trinket From The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Looks So Familiar

There are a lot of characters in the wider "Hunger Games" universe, so I'll forgive you if you're only familiar with some of the bigger players like Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence), Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada in his origin film and Woody Harrelson in the original movies), Coriolanus Snow (Tom Blyth, Ralph Fiennes, and Donald Sutherland at various points throughout his life), Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson), or Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler). The latest installment in the literary and cinematic franchise, "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," brings back some familiar faces and introduces new ones too — so, who, exactly, is Proserpina Trinket?

Introduced in both the book and film version of "Sunrise on the Reaping," Proserpina Trinket is a bubbly, enthusiastic, and quick-thinking young stylist working to prepare Hunger Games tributes for all the Capitol-centric pomp and circumstance that takes place before the bloody Games themselves. (Yes, the teenage tributes get all dolled up before they're forced to fight to the death in a dangerous arena that's also trying to kill them. This world is sick!)

We don't know a ton about Prosperina besides the fact that she works with the extremely unreliable Magno Stift (Billy Porter), she's assigned to work on Zada's Haymitch alongside Vitus (Edvin Ryding), and her older sister is future District 12 chaperone and stylist Effie Trinket (played in this film by Elle Fanning and the original movies by Elizabeth Banks). What we definitely know is that she's played by Iris Apatow, a rising talent from a famous family who's shown up in a handful of TV shows and several huge comedy movies from the 2000s.

Iris Apatow was born in 2002, and odds are you're familiar with her family. Her older sister, Maude Apatow, starred in "Euphoria" throughout its entire run. Her mother, Leslie Mann, is an acclaimed comedic actor. Then there's her dad Judd Apatow, a comedy kingmaker, producer, writer, and director who's helped make projects like "Superbad" and "Bridesmaids" and directed his own like "The 40-Year-Old Virgin," "Knocked Up," "Funny People," and "This is 40." Let's talk about those last three, because all of them feature the youngest Apatow. (The less said about Judd Apatow's 2022 COVID movie "The Bubble," the better.)

Maude and Iris Apatow play Sadie and Charlotte, respectively, in both "Knocked Up" and "This is 40" — with their on-screen mother, Debbie, portrayed by Mann, and their father Pete by Paul Rudd as an Apatow stand-in. As for "Funny People," they also play Mann's daughters (in this one, Maude is Mable and Iris is Ingrid) with Mann as Laura, the ex-girlfriend of comedian and actor George Simmons (Adam Sandler), who's dealing with a life-changing health crisis. Sure, the Apatow daughters don't do a ton here, but they flesh out the universe in all three of their dad's films ... and it's notable that we watched Maude and Iris grow up on-screen, basically.

All things considered, Iris Apatow's career is just getting started. Still, over the past few years, she's dabbled in more adult fare (especially on the small screen), so it definitely seems like she's trying to show off her range.

From 2016 to 2018, Apatow portrayed a supporting character, Arya Hopkins, who's tutored by series lead Gus (Paul Rust) on the Netflix TV show "Love," while on another Netflix exclusive, "Unstable," she appeared alongside Rob Lowe and his real-life son John Owen Love. The latter duo play tech CEO Ellis Dragon and his creatively inclined son Jackson, respectively, whereas Apatow plays Anna, an intern at Ellis' company, itself aptly named Dragon, who also happens to be the former stepdaughter of the company's CFO Anna ("Fleabag" standout Sian Clifford).

Then there's "Tell Me Lies." A deliciously dramatic and dishy Hulu series created by Meaghan Oppenheimer, "Tell Me Lies" adapts (and improves) the book of the same name by Carola Lovering and ran for three seasons on Hulu. Apatow shows up as a college student named Amanda in the third and final season, creating a problem for series regular Bree (Cat Missal) as she mentally and emotionally recovers from an affair with a professor named Oliver (Tom Ellis). After she finally gets out of Oliver's clutches, Bree notices that Amanda seems to be Oliver's next victim, sending her into a spiral.

You can see Apatow as Proserpina in "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" in theaters now.

It’s a very rare experience for me, but the year is almost over and I’m still talking about a movie that came out months ago on the 2026 release schedule: Obsession. I think it’s excellent on so many levels, but I particularly haven’t been able to get Inde Navarrette’s haunting performance as Nikki out of my head.

And, ever since I saw it, I’ve been saying I want to see Navarrette win an Oscar for it. As luck would have it, the breakthrough star is very much expected to get a nomination in the Best Actress category at this point in the race. But, now that I’ve seen her biggest competition in earning the golden trophy, wow, I have new thoughts to talk out.

I’ve been looking around at Oscar prediction sites, and while Inde Navarrette is quite high on the prediction list, there’s another actress always ahead of her: Julianne Moore for The Debut. And look, I like Moore, but she’s won an Oscar before and has been nominated a total of five times. She couldn’t possibly be better than Inde, I thought. Now that I’ve seen The Debut, I totally get why she’s so heavily favored now.

I don’t say movies are perfect too often, but The Debut is one of my few five-out-of-five ratings of the year. (Obsession and You Can See Everything are the other two). The movie comes from Jesse Eisenberg – who helped Kieran Culkin get his Oscar back in 2025 for his writing/directing effort, A Real Pain.

The Debut is a laugh-out-loud dark comedy about a woman named Mona, who is drained by living her life for her family. So, she decides to try out for a community play. Here’s the thing: she’s not very good, but when the original actress drops out during rehearsals, the director Jerry (played by Paul Giamatti) enlists her.

The Debut takes you through Mona’s chaotic journey as she attempts to understand what it really means to be an actress. I won’t get into too many details, but she completely gives herself over to the role in nuanced yet hilarious ways that has her slipping over the edge in a really entertaining way.

Oddly, there’s a transformation to it that’s not unlike what Navarrette did with Nikki. But, not only is Julianne Moore incredible as Mona, this feels like exactly the sort of performance that would appeal to Oscar voters because it’s literally about acting.

So, who am I rooting for now? I wish I could give it to both of them! While I’m more torn than I was before, I’d still like to see Inde Navarrette win that Oscar, the most honorable for what I think is a generational horror performance we’ll be talking about longer than The Debut.

While Moore is the frontrunner right now, with Gold Derby favoring Moore along with just about every prediction site, it’s still early in awards season. Moore is loved and respected by Hollywood, but it’s worth pointing out that Inde Navarrette’s likability and charm are off the charts. She could win over voters as the season goes on. But hey, I also didn’t think Amy Madigan’s Weapons performance would win at the 2026 Oscars, and she won! But now if The Debut wins, I won't be fuming, because Moore is truly so good, too!

The Oscars are on the 2027 winter TV schedule for Sunday, March 14. That’s four months from now. A lot could happen on the awards season trail. You can’t see The Debut in theaters quite yet, but it’s among upcoming A24 movies, with it set to hit theaters widely on Christmas Day. And Obsession is currently on Netflix.

#3580. Shannon Beador Reflects on Her Dog Archie’s Death in Heartbreaking Post

Shannon Beador shared a poignant post as she remembered her beloved late dog Archie ahead of the holiday season.

Posting via her Instagram on Friday, November 20, the Real Housewives of Orange County star, 62, shared a carousel of photos featuring Archie, who died in May.

“I’ve been wanting to post about Archie but it has been very difficult for me to put anything together. And as Thanksgiving approaches, it’s important for me to acknowledge how grateful my girls and I are for Archie’s presence in our lives,” Shannon wrote in the post’s lengthy caption..

She continued, “Archie passed away five days after our finale party was filmed. It happened so quickly. I was grateful that Stella was able to come home from Paris to say her goodbyes.”

Shannon went on to recall Archie’s final moments before he passed away shortly after his brain cancer diagnosis.

“Archie had been in the hospital and was so drugged, he couldn’t even stand up. We took him off all the medication and he spent his last day doing all of his favorite things,” she divulged. “Archie went to the beach, ate every type of food that he loved, and spent time sitting in the park.”

In May, Shannon shared the sad news of Archie’s death, which came nine days after the Bravo star announced her pet had been diagnosed with brain cancer.

“Heaven has a new special angel. Archie passed away yesterday and the girls and I are heartbroken. For the last 10 years, Archie wasn’t just my dog — he was my constant comfort, protector, best friend and truly the real “man” in my life,” she wrote.

Shannon continued: “I have been through so many highs and lows, and through every good time and every heartache, Archie was always by my side and loved me the same way every single day. Never judging me and always giving pure, loyal, and unconditional love.”

The reality star thanked her followers for their well wishes and added, “There is such a void in our household right now.”

In her earlier posts, Shannon, who adopted Archie in 2016, explained she was looking into treatments for Archie.

“I know my posts about my dogs are usually fun and silly, but today I wanted to share something more serious,” Shannon shared on May 5. “After experiencing multiple seizures, Archie has been diagnosed with brain cancer.”

She continued, “Our heart aches for our sweet Archie. He means the world to the girls and I. We are going to do everything we can to help him fight this.”
